paths.title: Write a CUDA kernel that is actually fast
paths.blurb: The shortest honest route from knowing C to knowing why your kernel is at 30 percent of peak.
paths.who: You can write CUDA that compiles and runs. You cannot yet say, before running it, whether a change will make it faster.

stages.title: What a memory access costs
stages.why: Every GPU performance problem is a memory problem wearing a costume. You cannot reason about coalescing without knowing what a cache line is and why it exists.

stages.title: What a float is
stages.why: Half the arithmetic on a modern accelerator is in a format that cannot represent 0.1, and the reason it works anyway is the subject here.

stages.title: What the cost model says
stages.why: Before the hardware, the arithmetic. A matrix multiply has a known ratio of flops to bytes, and that ratio decides everything downstream.

stages.title: The machine itself
stages.why: Now the part that is actually a GPU: what an SM is, what a warp does when threads disagree, and where the memory hierarchy differs from the one you know.

stages.title: Kernels people actually write
stages.why: A tiled matrix multiply, then the modern numeric formats, then attention. This is where the earlier units get spent.

paths.title: Build a computer from a transistor
paths.blurb: One switch, then one gate, then a machine that runs a program you wrote for it.
paths.who: You write software and have never been able to say where the hardware stops and the software starts.

stages.title: The switch
stages.why: Everything above rests on one device that leaks, costs energy to flip, and stopped getting better in a specific year for a specific reason.

stages.title: Logic, and then a machine
stages.why: One primitive gate, and then every part of a computer built from it, ending with the component that makes the pile of parts run a program.

stages.title: The same work, in a language a tool understands
stages.why: Hand-drawn netlists stop scaling. This is the same designs described to a synthesiser, and the first time a clock period is a number rather than an idea.

stages.title: What it can compute at all
stages.why: Having built one, the question of what any of them can and cannot do, which turns out to be answerable and not to depend on the hardware.

paths.title: Understand what your compiler did
paths.blurb: From the source you wrote to the instructions that ran, with nothing taken on faith.
paths.who: You read assembly occasionally and mostly guess. You want to stop guessing.

stages.title: The instruction set, for real
stages.why: Not the tutorial version. The registers, how an address is formed, what a system call actually is, and what a linker leaves behind.

stages.title: Why the same instructions run at different speeds
stages.why: Two programs with identical instruction counts differ by ten times, and the reason is never in the listing.

stages.title: The compiler's own middle
stages.why: The representation an optimiser actually works on, how instructions get chosen, and what a debugger has to be told to make any of it legible.

stages.title: Measuring instead of believing
stages.why: The last unit is the one that makes the rest usable: how to find out, rather than reason about, which of two versions is faster.

paths.title: Make something move
paths.blurb: The route to a machine with no operating system, a motor, and a deadline it cannot miss.
paths.who: You have written a control loop that mostly works and want to know why it sometimes does not.

stages.title: A computer with nothing under it
stages.why: No kernel, no allocator, no scheduler. What a program looks like when the hardware is the only thing beneath it.

stages.title: Turning the world into numbers
stages.why: A sensor reading is a voltage that was measured at particular moments, and every property of the signal you recover follows from when those moments were.

stages.title: The loop that has to close on time
stages.why: A deadline missed is a different failure from an answer that is wrong, and the units here are about the first kind.

stages.title: Deciding where to go
stages.why: Above the loop: geometry, a plan, and the point where a learned policy replaces the plan.
